Working notes:

- Do not default to option C. It was rejected for 9 of 10 tickets.
- The only confirmed successful assignment was C for a large invoice from the north region (REQ-2411), with “No rush, but please confirm receipt.”
- C was rejected for:
  - Claims (small/large), shipments (small/large), and refunds (large), across north/east/south.
  - A small invoice has not been tested.
- Region alone does not justify C; north-region requests were rejected when they were shipments or claims.
- Size alone does not justify C; large shipments, refunds, and claims were rejected.
- The successful case suggests C may be tied to invoice type and/or the low-urgency wording, but this is not yet proven.
- Prefer A or B for future cases unless the request matches a confirmed C pattern. Further testing should vary one attribute at a time, especially invoice vs. other request types and urgency wording.

Working notes:

- Do not default to C. It was rejected in prior tests and is now explicitly invalid for additional non-invoice requests.
- Confirmed successful C: large north-region invoice REQ-2411 with “No rush, but please confirm receipt.” This remains the only confirmed C success; invoice type and/or wording may matter, but the pattern is unproven.
- Region and size alone do not determine the assignment. Large east/south claims and shipments, and small claims/shipments/refunds across regions, have produced differing valid options.
- Newly observed A successes:
  - Large east claim (REQ-2415)
  - Large south shipment (REQ-2416)
  - Small south claim (REQ-2418)
- A was explicitly invalid for:
  - Small south shipment (REQ-2419)
  - Small north claim (REQ-2420)
  - Small east refund (REQ-2421)
  - Large south claim (REQ-2422)
- B was explicitly invalid for a small east shipment (REQ-2417). No confirmed B success is recorded.
- Treat each request as requiring a context-specific assignment; do not infer from region, size, or request type alone.
- Prefer the option supported by an exact prior match. Otherwise, use further testing to vary one attribute at a time, especially request type, size, region, and urgency/wording.

Working notes:

- Treat every request as context-specific; region, size, type, wording, sender, and urgency do not independently determine the assignment.
- Do not default to C. Earlier C successes: large north invoice REQ-2411 and large north refund REQ-2424. C was invalid for REQ-2433, REQ-2437, REQ-2438, and REQ-2439.
- A has several confirmed successes:
  - REQ-2415 large east claim
  - REQ-2416 large south shipment
  - REQ-2418 small south claim
  - REQ-2441 large east shipment
  - REQ-2447 large east invoice
  - REQ-2448 small south invoice
  - REQ-2449 large south invoice
  - REQ-2451 large east refund
  - REQ-2452 small south claim
- A remains invalid for REQ-2419, REQ-2420, REQ-2421, REQ-2422, REQ-2435, REQ-2436, REQ-2440, REQ-2442, and REQ-2450. Thus A is not reliably determined by type, region, size, or wording.
- B remains unconfirmed as a general rule; it was invalid for small east shipment REQ-2417. Recent logs include B trials, but do not establish a dependable pattern.
- D is not a valid option and has been rejected repeatedly; exclude it.
- Repeated wording can produce different assignments: “This one came in through the regional office” succeeded with A for REQ-2447 but A failed for REQ-2450. Exact matches are useful but not decisive.
- Test systematically, changing one attribute at a time, and record confirmed outcomes rather than inferring from malformed or ambiguous log chains.

Working notes:

- Treat every request as context-specific; region, size, type, wording, sender, and urgency do not independently determine the assignment.
- Do not default to C. Confirmed C successes include REQ-2411, REQ-2424, REQ-2453 (large north claim), REQ-2454 (small north refund), and REQ-2458 (large north shipment). C was invalid for REQ-2433, REQ-2437, REQ-2438, REQ-2439, REQ-2456, and REQ-2457.
- A has many confirmed successes, including REQ-2415, REQ-2416, REQ-2418, REQ-2441, REQ-2447, REQ-2448, REQ-2449, REQ-2451, REQ-2452, and REQ-2459 on some attempts. A remains invalid for REQ-2419–REQ-2422, REQ-2435, REQ-2436, REQ-2440, REQ-2442, REQ-2450, and REQ-2455.
- REQ-2459 produced alternating acceptance and rejection for the identical request and choice A. Therefore, logs may be nondeterministic, duplicated, or affected by hidden state; do not treat a single result as a stable rule.
- B remains unconfirmed as a general rule; it was invalid for small east shipment REQ-2417. No dependable pattern is established.
- D is not valid and should be excluded.
- Repeated wording is not decisive: “This one came in through the regional office” has yielded both A success and failure across requests—and even across repeated REQ-2459 attempts.
- Test systematically, change one attribute at a time where possible, and record confirmed outcomes while flagging contradictory or malformed chains.
